Package org.aeonbits.owner.loaders

Class IniLoader

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.loaders.IniLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Loader
public class IniLoader extends Object implements Loader
A loader for INI files: sections in square brackets, key = value below them. 
     [server]
     host = localhost
     port = 8080
 
     server.host=localhost
     server.port=8080

A section becomes the prefix of the keys below it, which needs no convention of its own: it is the same dot PropertyKeys already uses for nesting, so [a.b] and a nested structure produce the same keys, and keys written before any section have no prefix at all.

A repeated key is a list, numbered exactly as repeated XML elements are:

     [servers]
     host = alpha
     host = beta
 
     servers.host[0]=alpha
     servers.host[1]=beta

A key occurring once keeps its plain key, and only a repeat is numbered - at which point the first is moved to [0]. The asymmetry is the same one the XML loader has and for the same reason: when the first occurrence is read there is no telling whether a second will follow, and numbering everything on the chance of it would rename the keys of every file that has no repeats. IniDialect.Duplicates has the other answers, the field being divided three ways on this.

There is no INI standard, so the rules are an IniDialect, chosen the same two ways a .env dialect is - by registering the loader, or per source in the fragment: 

     @Sources("file:app.ini#dialect=git")

This loader accepts a source whose path ends in .ini or .cfg, and looks for both of those beside the configuration class when no @Sources is declared.

    • defaultSpecsFor

      public String[] defaultSpecsFor(String uriPrefix)
      Returns every default URI specification this loader offers, and is the one the library calls.

      The default answers with whatever Loader.defaultSpecFor(String) returned, so a loader with a single name has nothing to do here and a loader written before this method existed keeps working unchanged. Override this one, and not that one, when a format goes by several names: 

           @Override
     public String[] defaultSpecsFor(String uriPrefix) {
         return new String[] { uriPrefix + ".yaml", uriPrefix + ".yml" };
     }

      The order matters: these are tried in the order given, and under Config.LoadType.FIRST the first one that resolves is the one that answers. An empty array, like a null from the single-valued method, means this loader adds nothing.

      Both of the names the format goes by, which is what defaultSpecsFor(String) exists for.

      Specified by:
      defaultSpecsFor in interface Loader
      Parameters:
      uriPrefix - the prefix identifying the URI resource.
      Returns:
      the default URI specifications, in the order they should be tried; never containing null.
